messages:
marie: heads up — bringing up gpt-neoxt-20b (int4, grouped quant) on a dedicated pool. reproducible OOMs when batch_size >= 5 + prefetch=3. memory use jumps then CUDA OOMs after ~30s. anyone seen a similar fragmentation pattern?

devon: :eyes: saw something like this with grouped-int4 and kernel scratch allocs. fragmentation looked like lots of small GPU frees, jemalloc arenas on the host also contributed. try lowering prefetch and limiting max_new_tokens per request while we debug.

samir: attaching a short log excerpt — the OOM happens at allocation for new KV block. note the tail of the trace has many small free/alloc pairs.

samir: ```
[2026-03-19T18:02:12Z] Alloc 2.4G for kv_cache shard 3
[2026-03-19T18:02:13Z] Free 24M
[2026-03-19T18:02:13Z] Alloc 1.8G -> cudaGetLastError: out of memory
```

devon: for experiments try: batch_size=4, prefetch=1, max_new_tokens default=128 (we've seen 256->512 blow past fragmentation threshold). also enable periodic KV trimming: kv_trim_interval_s=30.

marie: trying that now. starting a small canary with those settings. will report latency regression if any.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: gneoxt-20b-int4 pool-id=gneoxt-ded-3 status=started commit=ae3f21 :rocket:

anya: quick workaround that helped before — in engine config set cuda_allow_growth=true and enable cuda_mem_compact=true (host-side compaction run every 60s). reduces peak fragmentation spikes. also try host malloc tuning: MALLOC_CONF=retain:false,oversize_threshold:1 to avoid holding many small arenas.

devon: good call. also watch runtime for 'kv_cache_evictions' metric — if evictions spike it's a sign trimming is too aggressive.

marie: canary ran for ~10m with batch_size=4 prefetch=1 max_new_tokens=128 and cuda_mem_compact enabled — no OOMs so far, perf within 8% of baseline. landing as temporary default for gneoxt-20b int4.

samir: created a short follow-up perf/eval ticket with checklist: reproduce w/ synthetic load, run nvprof for allocations, capture jemalloc stats, try compact intervals 30/60/120s, test max_new_tokens 64/128/256.

marie: thanks all. filing rollout note and bumping default in model-profile to: {"batch":4, "prefetch":1, "max_new_tokens":128, "kv_trim_interval_s":30, "cuda_mem_compact":true} :white_check_mark:
